sources.citation: Boyd, Raymond. n.d. [PDF dated 2016]. The phonology and tonology of Chamba Daka. Unpublished ms., Laboratoire Ligérien de Linguistique, Université d'Orléans. 45 pp. (Nnakennyaare dialect, Ganye, Adamawa State = Sama Mum / Samba Daka, samb1311, ISO ccg)
sources.note: Describes a sister/possibly same-cluster variety, NOT Lamja-Dengsa-Tola. No word-stress statement. p. 26 (§III.1.1): 'CN is a three-register language: it lexically contrasts high (H), mid (M), and low (L) tones... CN also has a phenomenon of tonal downstep'. Only stress mention is an analogy on p. 19 (§I.3): 'relative "weight" of canonic forms is used in CN in a way similar to stress in some toneless languages'. Lamja/Dengsa/Tola never mentioned.
